Theme

Work & responsibility

career noun

also choose a career, career change, walk of life, way of life, calling

classical

Cic. Off. 1.117: in quō genere vītae
Cic. Off. 1.120: in dēligendō genere vītae, in choosing a career

genus vītae

noun and genitive

a career, a walk of life

Cicero’s term for the life one chooses in early youth (Off. 1.117–121).

Other words

  • cursus, cursūs m. — the course of a career

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.117: certō genere cursūque vīvendī; Traupman 180: cursus honōrum, a political career · Declension on Wiktionary

    The political career, the ladder of offices, is cursus honōrum (cf. Cic. Fam. 3.11.2, Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • in prīmīs autem cōnstituendum est, quōs nōs et quālēs esse velīmus et in quō genere vītae, quae dēlīberātiō est omnium difficillima

    above all we must decide who and what kind of people we want to be, and in what career; and that is the hardest decision of allCic. Off. 1.117

See also job, trade, professional, position.
